city_placeholder: Search a city in English or 中文
city_not_found: City not in our list. Your coordinates still work; enter them below.
noStars: No targets match your view. Try changing the time or relaxing the filters.
eyebrow: A SMALL GUIDE TO A VERY BIG SKY
hero_description: Pick a place and a moment. Discover familiar stars, trace the patterns, and know exactly where to look.
location_denied: Location is unavailable. Choose a city or enter your coordinates.
coordinate_hint: North and east are positive. South and west are negative.
time_zone_hint: The time above belongs to this time zone, even when you browse from somewhere else.
min_alt_hint: 10° helps avoid trees, buildings, and haze near the horizon.
preview_empty: Choose a valid location and time to preview the sky.
how_title: A few stars. A familiar sky.
how_description: Start with the brightest landmarks and find your way from there.
how_location_body: A city or your coordinates tell us which part of the sky is yours.
how_time_body: The sky changes through the night. See it now or plan ahead.
how_look_body: Find a bright star, check its direction, and trace a nearby pattern.
footer_tagline: A little guidance for your next clear night.
results_description: Bright landmarks, familiar patterns, and a direction to start.
share_fallback: Copy this link to share the same place and moment:
daylight_note: These targets are above the horizon, but daylight hides most stars. Try a later time.
twilight_note: The sky is still bright. Start with the brightest stars; fainter ones appear as it gets darker.
dark_note: The Sun is well below the horizon. Clouds, moonlight, and light pollution still affect what you can see.
recommended_hint: A simple guide based on brightness and height above the horizon.
no_recommendations: No bright landmarks match these filters. Lower the minimum altitude or include fainter targets.
map_guide_body: The center is straight overhead (90°). The edge is the horizon (0°). East is on the left because you are looking up. Rotate the map to match the direction you face.
map_interaction: Drag to rotate · tap a star to find it in the list
map_accessible: Interactive sky map. Use the rotation slider to rotate, and the target list to select stars.
celestial_hint: An equatorial view centered on your zenith. Drag to explore and scroll to zoom. The bright points are your selected targets.
celestial_error: The celestial view could not load. The horizon view is still available.
table_hint: Select a target to highlight it on the map.
no_patterns: No complete patterns match these filters at this time.
pattern_hint: Shown only when every member is above your altitude limit and included by your brightness filter.
mag_explain: Smaller magnitude numbers mean brighter targets. A cluster's magnitude is its combined light.
altitude_explain: Altitude is height above the horizon: 0° at the horizon, 90° straight overhead.
azimuth_explain: Azimuth is measured clockwise from true north: N 0° · E 90° · S 180° · W 270°.
accuracy_note: A guide for finding bright stars. Positions include precession, but omit refraction and proper motion. Visibility depends on your surroundings.
invalid_description: This link has missing or invalid location, time, or filter settings. Choose a place and time to continue.
invalid_form: Enter valid coordinates, a time between 1900 and 2100, and a recognized time zone.
dst_gap: That local time does not exist because the clocks change. Choose another time.
dst_fold: This time occurs twice when the clocks change. The earlier occurrence will be used.
legacy_time: This older link has no UTC offset. Its time is interpreted in your browser's time zone.
